subject: Biology
title: Dolphins: Ocean Intellects
description: A quick, practical guide to Dolphins: Ocean Intellects.

hook.text: Dolphins call each other by unique signature whistles—they have names.

buildup.text: Bottlenose dolphins have large brains relative to body size and show self-awareness in mirror tests.

discovery.text: They cooperate with human fishermen in Brazil—driving fish into nets and sharing the catch.

twist.text: Dolphins sleep with half their brain at a time. One eye stays open watching for sharks.

climax.text: Complex social bonds, tool use, play behavior, and cultural learning make dolphins among the smartest animals.

punchline.text: They have names, use tools, and sleep with one eye open.

quiz.question: How do dolphins sleep?
options: With half their brain at a time, one eye open
They sleep on the ocean surface

details.summary: Dolphins exhibit some of the highest intelligence in the animal kingdom, demonstrating self-awareness, tool use, complex social bonds, and sophisticated communication. Their large brains relative to body size and intricate social structures rival those of great apes in complexity.
details.whyItMatters: Dolphin intelligence challenges assumptions about the uniqueness of primate cognition and raises ethical questions about their treatment in captivity and their vulnerability to fishing, pollution, and noise disturbance.
takeaways: Dolphins recognize themselves in mirrors, indicating self-awareness
Bottlenose dolphins use sponges as tools to protect their snouts while foraging
Each dolphin develops a unique signature whistle functioning as a name

faq.question: How smart are dolphins compared to other animals?
faq.answer: Dolphins have among the highest brain-to-body ratios of any animal. They pass the mirror self-recognition test, use tools, plan cooperatively, and learn complex behaviors. Their intelligence is comparable to great apes, though it evolved independently.

faq.question: How do dolphins communicate with each other?
faq.answer: Through a complex system of clicks, whistles, and body language. Each dolphin has a unique signature whistle used as an identity call. They can learn and remember other individuals' whistles for decades and use them to call specific companions.
